# Image composition owns initrd/UKI creation; RPM transactions never alter the ESP.
%global kernel_release 7.2.8-vale3
%global debug_package %{nil}
%global __strip /bin/true
%global __brp_strip %{nil}
%global __brp_strip_static_archive %{nil}
%global __brp_strip_comment_note %{nil}
%global __brp_strip_lto %{nil}

Name:           kernel-vale
Version:        7.2.8
Release:        3.vale%{?dist}
Summary:        Vale Linux kernel with the Star Labs topic queue
License:        GPL-2.0-only
URL:            https://www.kernel.org
Source0:        linux-7.2.8.tar.xz
Source1:        kernel-x86_64-fedora.config
Source2:        vale-kernel-patches.tar.gz
Source3:        series
Source4:        vale.fragment
Source5:        shipping.fragment
ExclusiveArch:  x86_64
BuildRequires:  bc
BuildRequires:  binutils
BuildRequires:  bison
BuildRequires:  dwarves
BuildRequires:  elfutils-devel
BuildRequires:  elfutils-libelf-devel
BuildRequires:  flex
BuildRequires:  gcc
BuildRequires:  make
BuildRequires:  openssl
BuildRequires:  openssl-devel
BuildRequires:  perl
BuildRequires:  python3
BuildRequires:  rust
BuildRequires:  rust-src
BuildRequires:  bindgen-cli
BuildRequires:  clang
BuildRequires:  llvm
BuildRequires:  lld
BuildRequires:  zstd
BuildRequires:  rsync
BuildRequires:  kmod
Provides:       kernel-uname-r = %{kernel_release}
Provides:       kernel = %{version}-%{release}
Requires:       linux-firmware

%description
Linux %{version} with the ordered Vale CFR, encrypted snapshot and hardware
patches. Fedora configuration retains SELinux; the image signs its UKI.

%prep
%setup -q -n linux-%{version}
tar -xf %{SOURCE2}
while IFS= read -r patch; do
    patch --batch --fuzz=0 -p1 < "$patch"
done < %{SOURCE3}
cp %{SOURCE1} .config
scripts/kconfig/merge_config.sh -m .config %{SOURCE4} %{SOURCE5}
make olddefconfig
[ "$(make -s LOCALVERSION= kernelrelease)" = "%{kernel_release}" ]
grep -qx 'CONFIG_SECURITY_SELINUX=y' .config
grep -q '^CONFIG_LSM=.*selinux' .config
grep -qx 'CONFIG_ENCRYPTED_HIBERNATION=y' .config
grep -qx 'CONFIG_MODULE_COMPRESS_ALL=y' .config
grep -qx 'CONFIG_MODULE_COMPRESS_ZSTD=y' .config

%build
make %{?_smp_mflags} LOCALVERSION= KBUILD_BUILD_USER=vale KBUILD_BUILD_HOST=fedora44

%install
mkdir -p %{buildroot}%{_prefix}/lib/modules/%{kernel_release}
make LOCALVERSION= INSTALL_MOD_PATH=%{buildroot}%{_prefix} INSTALL_MOD_STRIP=1 DEPMOD=true modules_install
rm -f %{buildroot}%{_prefix}/lib/modules/%{kernel_release}/{build,source}
install -pm0644 arch/x86/boot/bzImage %{buildroot}%{_prefix}/lib/modules/%{kernel_release}/vmlinuz
install -pm0644 System.map %{buildroot}%{_prefix}/lib/modules/%{kernel_release}/System.map
install -pm0644 .config %{buildroot}%{_prefix}/lib/modules/%{kernel_release}/config
depmod -b %{buildroot} -m %{_prefix}/lib/modules -F System.map %{kernel_release}

%files
%license COPYING
%{_prefix}/lib/modules/%{kernel_release}/

image/fedora44/assemble-iso.sh.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Run inside mkosi's Fedora tools tree with the frozen native signing inputs.
: "${VALE_SECURE_BOOT_KEY:?set the Secure Boot private key}"
: "${VALE_SECURE_BOOT_CERT:?set the Secure Boot certificate}"
[[ $# -eq 1 ]]
worktree=$(realpath "$1")
version=$(cat "$worktree/mkosi.version")
[[ $version =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
cd "$worktree/mkosi.output"
live=liveiso_${version}
raw=elementary_${version}.raw
output=vale-fedora44-x86-64.${version}.iso
[[ ! -e $output ]]
work=$(mktemp -d .vale-iso.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

[[ -d $live && -f $raw && -f vale-live.initrd && -f vale-live.vmlinuz ]]
install -d "$work/iso/live" "$work/iso/extra" "$work/raw"
"$worktree/stage-installed-boot.sh" "$raw" "elementary-dave_${version}.efi"
mksquashfs "$live" "$work/iso/live/filesystem.squashfs" -comp zstd -noappend
# The native backend consumes one raw image inside its existing squashfs capsule.
cp --reflink=auto "$raw" "$work/raw/$raw"
mksquashfs "$work/raw" "$work/iso/extra/${raw}.squashfs" -comp zstd -noappend
os_release=$live/usr/lib/os-release
kernel_version=$(cat vale-live.uname)
[[ $kernel_version == 7.2.8-vale3 ]]
xorriso -as mkisofs -iso-level 3 -volid "VALE_FEDORA44" \
    -output "${work}/source.iso" "${work}/iso"
truncate -s 512M "${work}/esp.img"
mkfs.vfat -n VALEINSTALL "${work}/esp.img"
mmd -i "${work}/esp.img" ::/EFI ::/EFI/BOOT
truncate -s 128M "${work}/verity.img"
printf 'Vale authenticated installer\n' > "${work}/marker"

make_layout() {
    unlink "${work}/candidate.iso" 2>/dev/null || true
    xorriso -indev "${work}/source.iso" -outdev "${work}/candidate.iso" \
        -map "${work}/marker" /VALE-SIGNED-USB \
        -boot_image any discard \
        -boot_image any system_area=/dev/zero \
        -boot_image any appended_part_as=gpt \
        -append_partition 2 0xef "${work}/esp.img" \
        -append_partition 3 0x83 "${work}/verity.img" \
        -boot_image any efi_path=--interval:appended_partition_2:all::
}

make_layout
partition_end=$(sgdisk -i 1 "${work}/candidate.iso" |
    awk '/Last sector:/ { print $3 }')
if (( (partition_end + 1) % 4 != 0 )); then
    truncate -s +2048 "${work}/marker"
    make_layout
    partition_end=$(sgdisk -i 1 "${work}/candidate.iso" |
        awk '/Last sector:/ { print $3 }')
fi
esp_start=$(sgdisk -i 2 "${work}/candidate.iso" |
    awk '/First sector:/ { print $3 }')
hash_start=$(sgdisk -i 3 "${work}/candidate.iso" |
    awk '/First sector:/ { print $3 }')
hash_partuuid=$(sgdisk -i 3 "${work}/candidate.iso" |
    awk '/Partition unique GUID:/ { print tolower($4) }')
[[ ${partition_end}${esp_start}${hash_start} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
[[ ${hash_partuuid} =~ ^[0-9a-f-]{36}$ ]]
(( (partition_end + 1) % 4 == 0 && hash_start % 4 == 0 ))

data_blocks=$(((partition_end + 1) / 4))
hash_start_block=$((hash_start / 4))
salt=$(sha256sum "${raw}" | cut -d' ' -f1)
dd if="${work}/candidate.iso" of="${work}/data.img" bs=2048 \
    count="${data_blocks}" iflag=fullblock status=none
verity_output=$(veritysetup format --no-superblock \
    --data-block-size=2048 --hash-block-size=2048 --salt="${salt}" \
    "${work}/data.img" "${work}/verity.img")
root_hash=$(awk '/Root hash:/ { print $3 }' <<<"${verity_output}")
[[ ${root_hash} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]
dd if="${work}/verity.img" of="${work}/candidate.iso" bs=512 \
    seek="${hash_start}" conv=notrunc status=none

stub="${live}/usr/lib/systemd/boot/efi/linuxx64.efi.stub"
[[ -s ${stub} ]]

cmdline="boot=vale-live root=live:/dev/mapper/vale-install-media live-media=/dev/mapper/vale-install-media rd.live.dir=live rd.live.squashimg=filesystem.squashfs rd.live.overlay.overlayfs=1 rd.live.overlay.readonly=1 ro rd.shell=0 rd.emergency=poweroff selinux=1 enforcing=1 systemd.swap=no panic=-1 quiet splash i915.force_probe=!7d51,!7d55 xe.force_probe=7d51,7d55 vale.media_data_blocks=${data_blocks} vale.media_hash_partuuid=${hash_partuuid} vale.media_hash_start_block=${hash_start_block} vale.media_root_hash=${root_hash} vale.media_salt=${salt}"
ukify=$(realpath ../.vale/bin/ukify.real)
[[ -f ${ukify} && -x ${ukify} ]]
verifier=$(realpath ../.vale/bin/verify-vale-uki.py)
sbat=$(realpath ../.vale/bin/sbat.vale.csv)
VALE_PCR_TOOLS=/usr/lib/systemd
: "${VALE_PCR_RECOVERY_KEY:?set the independent recovery signing key}"
: "${VALE_PCR_RECOVERY_CERT:?set the independent recovery certificate}"
: "${VALE_PCR_RECOVERY_PUBLIC_KEY:?set the independent recovery public key}"
# Check the pinned stock tools before ukify can select a fallback.
python3 - "${verifier}" "${ukify}" "${VALE_PCR_TOOLS}" "${stub}" "${sbat}" <<'PY_TOOLS'
import runpy
import sys
from pathlib import Path
v = runpy.run_path(sys.argv[1])
v["native_inputs"](*(Path(value) for value in sys.argv[2:]))
PY_TOOLS
for purpose in normal-recovery dave-recovery; do
    printf '%s' "${cmdline} vale.mode=${purpose}" > "${work}/${purpose}.cmdline"
    pcr=()
    public=()
    if [[ ${purpose} == dave-recovery ]]; then
        pcr=(--pcr-banks sha256 --pcrpkey "${VALE_PCR_RECOVERY_PUBLIC_KEY}"
             --pcr-private-key "${VALE_PCR_RECOVERY_KEY}"
             --pcr-certificate "${VALE_PCR_RECOVERY_CERT}" --phases sysinit:ready
             --tools "${VALE_PCR_TOOLS}")
        public=(--recovery-key "${VALE_PCR_RECOVERY_PUBLIC_KEY}"
                --runtime-key "${VALE_PCR_POLICY_PUBLIC_KEY}"
                --initrd-key "${VALE_PCR_INITRD_PUBLIC_KEY}")
    fi
    "${ukify}" build --stub "${stub}" --sbat "@${sbat}" \
        --linux vale-live.vmlinuz --initrd vale-live.initrd --no-sign-kernel \
        --os-release "@${os_release}" --uname "${kernel_version}" \
        --cmdline "@${work}/${purpose}.cmdline" "${pcr[@]}" \
        --secureboot-private-key "${VALE_SECURE_BOOT_KEY}" \
        --secureboot-certificate "${VALE_SECURE_BOOT_CERT}" \
        --output "${work}/${purpose}.efi"
    "${verifier}" "${work}/${purpose}.efi" --purpose "${purpose}" \
        --cmdline "${work}/${purpose}.cmdline" --sb-cert "${VALE_SECURE_BOOT_CERT}" \
        "${public[@]}"
done
# The parent's signed public dispatch uses the literal BIOS vendor admission.
: "${VALE_RECOVERY_DISPATCH:?set the reviewed signed firmware-selected recovery dispatch}"
sbverify --cert "$VALE_SECURE_BOOT_CERT" "$VALE_RECOVERY_DISPATCH"
mmd -i "$work/candidate.iso@@$((esp_start * 512))" ::/EFI/Vale
mcopy -o -i "$work/candidate.iso@@$((esp_start * 512))" \
    "$work/dave-recovery.efi" ::/EFI/Vale/Dave.efi
mcopy -o -i "$work/candidate.iso@@$((esp_start * 512))" \
    "$work/normal-recovery.efi" ::/EFI/Vale/Normal.efi
mcopy -o -i "$work/candidate.iso@@$((esp_start * 512))" \
    "$VALE_RECOVERY_DISPATCH" ::/EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI
openssl x509 -in "${VALE_SECURE_BOOT_CERT}" -outform DER \
    -out "${work}/vale-secure-boot.cer"
mcopy -o -i "${work}/candidate.iso@@$((esp_start * 512))" \
    "${work}/vale-secure-boot.cer" ::/vale-secure-boot.cer

mv -T "${work}/candidate.iso" "${output}"
sha256sum "${output}"

scripts/build-recovery-dispatch.sh.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
repo=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
output=${1:?usage: build-recovery-dispatch.sh OUTPUT_DIRECTORY}
mkdir -p "${output}"
output=$(realpath "${output}")
sdk=$(podman image inspect localhost/vale-shim:16.1 --format '{{.Id}}')
printf '%s\n' "${sdk}" > "${output}/sdk-image-id"
podman run --rm -i --pull=never --network none --read-only --cap-drop all \
    --security-opt no-new-privileges --tmpfs /tmp:rw,nosuid,nodev \
    -v "${repo}/elementary/installer/recovery-dispatch:/source:ro" \
    -v "${output}:/output:rw" "${sdk}" bash -s <<'BUILD'
set -euo pipefail
cd /output
efi=/build/gnu-efi
flags=(-std=c11 -DGNU_EFI_USE_MS_ABI -I "$efi/inc" -I "$efi/inc/x86_64"
       -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fshort-wchar -mno-red-zone -maccumulate-outgoing-args)
gcc "${flags[@]}" -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer \
    /source/test-dispatch.c /source/dispatch.c /source/smbios.c -o test-dispatch
./test-dispatch
for unit in dispatch smbios; do
    gcc "${flags[@]}" -O2 -fpic -ffreestanding -fno-stack-protector \
        -fno-strict-aliasing -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables \
        -c "/source/$unit.c" -o "$unit.o"
done
ld -nostdlib -znocombreloc --build-id=none -T "$efi/gnuefi/elf_x86_64_efi.lds" \
    -shared -Bsymbolic "$efi/x86_64/gnuefi/crt0-efi-x86_64.o" dispatch.o smbios.o \
    /build/lib/string.o \
    -L "$efi/x86_64/lib" -L "$efi/x86_64/gnuefi" -lefi -lgnuefi \
    -o recovery-dispatch.so
if nm -u recovery-dispatch.so | grep .; then
    echo 'Unresolved EFI symbols' >&2
    exit 1
fi
objcopy -j .text -j .sdata -j .data -j .rodata -j .sbat -j .dynamic -j .dynsym \
    -j .rel -j .rela -j .reloc --strip-all -O pei-x86-64 --subsystem=10 \
    recovery-dispatch.so recovery-dispatch.efi
/build/post-process-pe -n -x recovery-dispatch.efi
objdump -p recovery-dispatch.efi
sha256sum recovery-dispatch.efi
BUILD

%global version_override 259.5
# We ship a .pc file but don't want to have a dep on pkg-config. We
# strip the automatically generated dep here and instead co-own the
# directory.
%global __requires_exclude pkg-config

%global pkgdir %{_prefix}/lib/systemd
%global system_unit_dir %{pkgdir}/system
%global user_unit_dir %{pkgdir}/user

%if 0%{?__isa_bits} == 64
%global elf_bits (64bit)
%global elf_suffix ()%{elf_bits}
%endif

%bcond bzip2     1
%bcond gnutls    1
%bcond lz4       1
%bcond xz        1
%bcond zlib      1
%bcond zstd      1

# Bootstrap may be needed to break circular dependencies with cryptsetup,
# e.g. when re-building cryptsetup on a json-c SONAME-bump.
%bcond bootstrap 0
%bcond tests     1

# riscv64 has LTO disabled globally
%bcond lto       %["%_arch" != "riscv64"]

# Build docs on 64-bit architectures only
%bcond docs      %[%{?__isa_bits} >= 64]

# Build from git main
%bcond upstream  0

# Build with OBS-specific quirks
%bcond obs       0

# When bootstrap, libcryptsetup is disabled
# but auto-features causes many options to be turned on
# that depend on libcryptsetup (e.g. libcryptsetup-plugins, homed)
%if %{with bootstrap}
%global __meson_auto_features disabled
# If we're building for upstream, don't unconditionally enable all
# new features as new features might be introduced for which we're
# missing build dependencies.
%elif %{with upstream}
%global __meson_auto_features auto
%endif

# Override %%autorelease. This is ugly, but rpmautospec doesn't implement
# autorelease correctly if the macro is conditionalized in the Release field.
%{?release_override:%global autorelease %{release_override}%{?dist}}

# In OBS, noarch packages are shared between all architectures and
# independent architectures can be rebuilt automatically without all
# the other architectures getting rebuilt. This can result in the noarch
# packages being newer than the archful packages for some architectures,
# which means our current strict deps from the noarch packages on the
# archful packages can't be satisfied.
#
# To address this problem, let's relax the dependencies from the noarch
# packages on the archful packages for OBS builds. Let's only do this for
# OBS builds because this isn't an issue on Fedora as it's impossible to
# build a package for only some of the architectures.
%if %{with obs}
%define noarch_requires_version %{version}
%else
%define noarch_requires_version %{version}-%{release}
%endif

Name:           systemd
Url:            https://systemd.io
# Allow users to specify the version and release when building the rpm by
# setting the %%version_override and %%release_override macros.
# But don't do that on OBS, otherwise the version subst fails, and will be
# like 257-123-gabcd257.1 instead of 257-123-gabcd
%if %{without obs}
Version:        %{?version_override}%{!?version_override:259.9}
%else
Version:        %{?version_override}%{!?version_override:%(cat meson.version)}
%endif
Release:        2.vale%{?dist}

# download tarballs with "spectool -g systemd.spec"

%if %{undefined branch} && %{undefined commit} && %{without obs}

# This file must be available before %%prep.
# It is generated during systemd build and can be found at build/src/rpm/triggers.systemd.sh.

Source8:        systemd-journal-remote.xml

# https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/How_to_filter_libabigail_reports

Source26:       systemd-user

%if 0%{?fedora} < 40 && 0%{?rhel} < 10
# Work-around for dracut issue: run generators directly when we are in initrd
# https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2164404

%if %{without upstream}
# Those are downstream-only patches, but we don't want them in packit builds.

%description
systemd is a system and service manager that runs as PID 1 and starts the rest
of the system. It provides aggressive parallelization capabilities, uses socket
and D-Bus activation for starting services, offers on-demand starting of
daemons, keeps track of processes using Linux control groups, maintains mount
and automount points, and implements an elaborate transactional dependency-based
service control logic. systemd supports SysV and LSB init scripts and works as a
replacement for sysvinit. Other parts of this package are a logging daemon,
utilities to control basic system configuration like the hostname, date, locale,
maintain a list of logged-in users, system accounts, runtime directories and
settings, and a logging daemons.

# above does not do this, because the line is marked with ! and
# tmpfiles is invoked without --boot in the scriptlet.)
#
# *Create* the symlink if nothing is present yet.
# (https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2032085)
#
# *Override* the symlink if systemd is running. Don't do it if systemd
# is not running, because that will immediately break DNS resolution,
# since systemd-resolved is also not running
# (https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1891847).
#
# Also don't create the symlink to the stub when the stub is disabled (#1891847 again).
if systemctl -q is-enabled systemd-resolved.service &>/dev/null &&
   ! systemd-analyze cat-config systemd/resolved.conf 2>/dev/null |
        grep -iqE '^DNSStubListener\s*=\s*(no?|false|0|off)\s*$'; then

  if ! test -e /etc/resolv.conf && ! test -L /etc/resolv.conf; then
    ln -sv ../run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf /etc/resolv.conf || :
  elif test -d /run/systemd/system/ &&
     ! mountpoint /etc/resolv.conf &>/dev/null; then
    ln -fsv ../run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf /etc/resolv.conf || :
  fi
fi
